content.user_title: Define Software Work Before You Build
content.value_statement: Ambiguous requirements cause rework, scope drift, and weak acceptance criteria. This skill creates reviewed specifications, plans, and tasks before implementation begins.
actual_capabilities: Identifies assumptions and asks clarifying questions before drafting a specification.
Decomposes multi-capability initiatives into modules with stable identifiers, dependencies, and build order.
Produces specifications covering objectives, commands, structure, style, testing, boundaries, and success criteria.
Converts approved specifications into dependency-aware implementation plans and reviewable tasks.
Defines human approval gates between specification, planning, task creation, and implementation.
Supports existing specification formats such as OpenSpec without duplicating artifacts.
limitations: Requires human review and approval at each workflow gate.
Does not replace domain expertise or independently validate business assumptions.
Depends on separate skills for detailed planning, testing, context management, and implementation.
Adds unnecessary process for typo fixes and other small, unambiguous changes.

use_cases.title: Clarify a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn an incomplete feature request into measurable requirements, boundaries, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Map a Complex Initiative
use_cases.description: Split a broad initiative into independently testable modules with explicit dependencies and delivery order.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Work
use_cases.description: Create an approved technical plan and small, verifiable tasks before changing the codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Feature Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a specification for [feature]. First list assumptions and ask questions about users, scope, constraints, and measurable success.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a single feature request is incomplete.

prompt_templates.title: Reframe Vague Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these requirements into specific acceptance criteria: [requirements]. Identify unresolved assumptions and propose measurable targets for human approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when desired outcomes are subjective or unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Capability Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [initiative]. Propose stable module identifiers, responsibilities, dependencies, interfaces, and build order. Stop for approval before writing module specifications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when one initiative contains several independently testable capabilities.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Approved Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the approved specification [location], create a dependency-aware implementation plan and tasks. Include risks, file scope, acceptance criteria, and verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a reviewed specification is ready for delivery planning.

output: Objective: Improve dashboard loading for users on constrained mobile connections.
Success: Largest Contentful Paint stays below 2.5 seconds on the agreed test profile.
Open question: Confirm the target device, network profile, and measurement environment.

output_examples.input: Decompose an account, billing, notification, and reporting initiative.
output: Billing depends on identity; notifications also depend on identity.
Reporting follows billing and notifications after their interfaces are approved.

output_examples.input: Create a task from an approved authentication plan.
output: Task: Add session validation at protected route boundaries.
Acceptance: Invalid sessions receive the approved unauthorized response.
Verification: Run focused route tests, then the full test suite.

best_practices: State assumptions before writing requirements and resolve important ambiguity with the human reviewer.
Keep success criteria measurable, testable, and linked to user or system outcomes.
Update the specification when decisions or scope change, then reference it during implementation and review.
anti_patterns: Do not start implementation before the relevant specification and plan receive approval.
Do not combine independently testable capabilities into one oversized specification.
Do not treat commands, boundaries, or verification steps as implied project knowledge.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for new projects, substantial features, unclear requirements, architectural decisions, or changes spanning several files or modules.

faq.question: When should I skip it?
faq.answer: Skip it for typo corrections, single-line fixes, and other small changes with complete, unambiguous requirements.

faq.question: Does it write implementation code?
faq.answer: It prepares and gates implementation, then delegates detailed execution to separate implementation and testing skills.

faq.question: Can it use an existing specification system?
faq.answer: Yes. It preserves established formats and storage conventions, including OpenSpec, while applying clarification and approval gates.

faq.question: How does it handle large initiatives?
faq.answer: It proposes a capability map with stable module identifiers, responsibilities, dependencies, interfaces, and build order before creating module specifications.

faq.question: What must a complete specification include?
faq.answer: It covers objectives, technology, commands, project structure, code style, testing, boundaries, measurable success criteria, and open questions.
